newsitem.title: USA: Telmex ADR hits year high, volume heavy.
newsitem.headline: Telmex ADR hits year high, volume heavy.

text.p: American Depositary Receipts of Telefonos de Mexico, or Telmex, hit a 12-month high on Wednesday in heavy trade.

ADRs in the Mexican telephone company closed up 1-1/8 at a 41-5/8 record. Almost 5.3 million ADRs were traded, more than twice the daily volume, and Telmex was the fifth most-active shares on the New York Stock Exchange.

In Mexico, Telmex closed at all-time record in peso terms, with its L shares up 48 centavos at 16.58 pesos. However, traders noted that in dollar terms, Telmex remained below its pre-1994 devaluation levels, when its ADR traded over 70.
Traders said there was no company news to boost ADRs. They were helped in part by short-covering from investors who had bet that the stock would go down.
"It's too many shorts in the market. The stock has been very difficult to borrow," said Lucia Skwarek, head of Latin American equities at UBS Securities.
Traders also said the surge was a follow-through on Tuesday buying and a result of improved Mexican economic news, including a drop in the overnight Cetes interest rate and a stronger peso.
Mexican stocks overall were helped by news the U.S. Senate planned to rebuke rather than decertify Mexico's anti-drug efforts and by an improvement in the jobless rate.
